questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

questions.stem: According to the text, what accounts for the different colours anthocyanins produce?

questions.passage: The red of a poppy petal and the blue of a cornflower are built from the same class of molecule. A gardener who limes the soil under a hydrangea does not give the plant a different pigment; the pigment it already has behaves differently.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how the guillotine changed the order in which a book is made. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • A binder trimmed a book's edges with a plough, a knife drawn across the closed leaves in a press.
  • The plough cuts a few leaves at a time and takes several minutes for one book.
  • The guillotine, introduced in the 1830s, cuts a stack of several hundred sheets at one stroke.
  • Sheets can be guillotined before they are sewn.
  • A book trimmed with a plough can be trimmed again only by losing more of its margins.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The guillotine was introduced in the 1830s and cuts a stack of several hundred sheets at one stroke.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A book trimmed with a plough can be trimmed again only by losing more of its margins.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Because the guillotine cuts several hundred sheets at one stroke, trimming could be done before the sheets were sewn rather than after the book was bound.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The plough cuts a few leaves at a time and takes several minutes to trim one book.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain what after-images suggest about the handling of colour signals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Stare at a red patch for half a minute and then look at white paper: a green patch appears.
  • The colour of an after-image is always the opposite of the colour stared at.
  • Three kinds of cone by themselves do not explain why the pairs are red-green and blue-yellow.
  • Cells further back in the visual system respond to the difference between cone signals.
  • Such a cell is excited by one colour of a pair and inhibited by the other.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Staring at a red patch for half a minute produces a green after-image on white paper.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The human retina contains three kinds of cone, and after-images appear when the eye is turned to a white surface.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Cells in the visual system are excited by one colour and inhibited by another.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Because an after-image is always the opposite of the colour stared at, colour cannot be handled by the cone types alone: cells further back respond to the difference between cone signals, excited by one colour of a pair and inhibited by the other.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain to an audience already familiar with dyeing why the bran and madder are added. Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While working on a paragraph, a student has written the following sentences:
  • A woad vat is set with bran and madder as well as with the woad itself.
  • The bran and madder feed bacteria that strip the oxygen out of the liquor.
  • Only once the oxygen has gone does the blue become soluble.
  • A vat that has stopped working is said to have died.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Bacteria in a woad vat consume the bran and madder that are added to it.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The bran and madder feed bacteria that strip the oxygen out of the liquor, and only once the oxygen has gone does the blue become soluble.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A woad vat is set with bran and madder as well as with the woad itself, and a vat that has stopped working is said to have died.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A woad vat contains three things: woad, bran and madder.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Feathers carrying melanin wear far more slowly than white ones, which is why the wingtips of many gulls are black although the rest of the bird is not. The pigment does not merely colour the barbs: it packs into them and leaves them harder and stiffer, and a worn black tip is rarer than a worn white one on the same wing. Black at the wingtip is therefore best explained as _____.

questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “agree” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Two pieces of cloth dyed with different mixtures can match exactly under a shop's lamps and differ unmistakably at the window. The eye reports only three signals, and two different spectra can produce the same three. A buyer who checks a match under one light has learned nothing about how the two pieces will <u>agree</u> under another.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Wool is a protein fibre carrying places along its length that will bond with an acid dye directly, and an hour in a warm bath with a little acid colours it through. Cotton is cellulose and offers such a dye almost nothing, which is why cotton dyers turn to dyes that either lodge inside the fibre or form a chemical bond with it. The two fibres differ less in how deeply they can be coloured than in what the colour must find to _____.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A film of linseed oil left on glass does not dry as a puddle of water dries. It gains weight while it hardens, because what is happening is a reaction with oxygen from the air that links the molecules of the oil into a network. Nothing evaporates, and the film cannot afterwards be dissolved in the oil it was made from. To call such a paint dry is therefore _____.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A pigment ground finer covers more ground, but grinding can go too far: coarse azurite is a deep blue, and the same mineral reduced to a flour is pale. There is no number of turns that settles the question, because it differs with the mineral and with the oil. The colourman lifts the muller, looks and decides, so where the grinding should stop is a matter of _____.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A hand mould covered in woven wire leaves no mark in the sheet formed on it. An older laid mould carries stout wooden ribs with fine wires running across them, and the pulp settles more thinly over every wire than beside it. <u>Hold a laid sheet up to a window and the ribs and wires appear as a ladder of lighter and darker lines.</u> Nothing has been printed on the paper; the pattern is a difference in thickness.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It explains why laid moulds were given up in favour of woven ones.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It corrects a mistaken account of how the pattern is produced.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It introduces a second method of forming a sheet by hand.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It offers a way of observing the difference the text has just described.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A reader of a scroll who wants a passage in the middle must unwind everything before it and wind it up again afterwards, and can hold only one place at a time. A reader of a codex opens the boards at any leaf, keeps a finger in a second place, and moves between the two. The codex holds no more text than the roll it displaced and is no easier to make.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To describe in detail how a codex is bound.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To establish when the codex replaced the scroll.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To account for the adoption of a format in terms of what it allowed a reader to do.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To argue that scrolls were more poorly made than codices.

questions.stem: According to the text, what does the separation on the paper strip establish about a dye?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A drop of a dye mixture placed near the end of a paper strip and stood in solvent separates as the solvent climbs: each component travels at a rate set by how strongly it clings to the paper against how readily it dissolves. A dye sold as one colour may resolve into four bands. The strip shows nothing about what those components are, only that they are several and in what proportion.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Whether its colour will fade in strong sunlight.

choices.label: B
choices.content: How strongly it will bind to a length of cloth.

choices.label: C
choices.content: How many components it contains and in what proportion, but not what they are.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The chemical identity of each of its components.

questions.stem: According to the text, why did ground lapis lazuli have to be treated further before it could be used as a pigment?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Ground lapis lazuli yields a dull grey powder, because the rock is mostly colourless mineral with the blue scattered through it. The colour was recovered by kneading the powder into a paste of wax and resin under warm lye: the blue particles passed into the water while the rest stayed behind in the paste. Three washings gave three grades, the first the richest and the last nearly grey, and the price of the pigment followed the yield of the first washing.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The blue faded unless it had first been washed in lye.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The wax and resin deepened the colour of the powder.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The blue mineral in it was mixed with a great deal of colourless material.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The rock could not otherwise be ground fine enough to use.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Halloran's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Marbled papers are often attributed to particular workshops on the strength of their patterns. Conservator Ines Halloran argues that such attributions can be put on a firmer footing, because the spacing of the teeth on a workshop's comb is fixed and shows in the spacing of the lines drawn through the floating colour.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Combs were usually made by the marblers themselves rather than bought from a supplier.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The same pattern names were used by workshops in several different countries.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Sheets from two workshops known to have worked to the same pattern name were found to differ consistently in the spacing of the lines drawn through the colour.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Marbled papers made in the same workshop often use the same range of colours.

questions.passage: The human eye carries three kinds of cone; a starling's carries four, the extra one sensitive in the ultraviolet. A human observer sorting the birds by plumage alone would therefore _____

choices.label: B
choices.content: be unable to tell the birds apart by any means whatever.

choices.label: C
choices.content: find the two sexes easier to distinguish than another starling does.

choices.label: D
choices.content: be right to conclude that the feathers reflect no ultraviolet.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

questions.passage: Vellum takes up water from the air and gives it back again, and a leaf that has done so many times no longer lies flat. A medieval binding holds its text block closed between two boards under the pressure of a clasp, and volumes that have stayed clasped for five centuries open with their leaves still flat. Volumes whose clasps were stripped off in the nineteenth century have leaves that cockle. The clasp is therefore best understood as _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: a device for holding the wooden boards themselves flat.

choices.label: B
choices.content: a means of keeping the leaves under a pressure they need.

choices.label: C
choices.content: a fastening meant to stop others from opening the book.

choices.label: D
choices.content: a decorative fitting whose loss makes no practical difference.

questions.stem: The student wants to emphasise the practical change the 1931 definition brought about. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Before 1931 a colour could be specified only by naming or sending a physical sample.
  • Samples fade, and two people may disagree about whether two samples match.
  • In 1931 an international body defined an average observer from matching experiments with a few dozen people.
  • A colour could then be stated as three numbers worked out from its spectrum.
  • Two dyers in different countries could specify one colour without exchanging anything physical.

choices.label: A
choices.content: An international body met in 1931 and defined an average observer.

choices.label: B
choices.content: By defining an average observer, the 1931 standard allowed a colour to be stated as three numbers worked out from its spectrum, so that two dyers in different countries could specify one colour without exchanging anything physical.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The 1931 standard observer was defined from matching experiments carried out with a few dozen people.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Before 1931 a colour could be specified only by naming or sending a physical sample, and samples fade.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how a retarding agent improves an uneven dyeing. Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to accomplish this goal?

questions.passage:
While working on a paragraph, a student has written the following sentences:
  • A dye that strikes the fibre very quickly colours the first part of the cloth it meets most deeply.
  • The finished piece is then blotchy rather than evenly coloured.
  • A retarding agent added to the bath competes with the dye for places on the fibre.
  • The dye attaches more slowly and spreads through the cloth before it fixes.

choices.label: A
choices.content: A dye that strikes the fibre very quickly gives a blotchy piece rather than an evenly coloured one.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A retarding agent is added to the dye bath before the cloth goes in.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Dyes attach themselves to places on the surface of the fibre.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A retarding agent competes with the dye for places on the fibre, so the dye attaches more slowly and spreads through the cloth before it fixes instead of colouring the first part it meets most deeply.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how adding a blue pigment can make a sheet look whiter. Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to accomplish this goal?

  • The blue does not remove the yellow; it absorbs a little more of the light that the yellow cast returns.
  • The sheet reflects less light overall and yet is judged whiter.

choices.label: A
choices.content: A trace of blue does not remove the sheet's yellow cast but absorbs some of the light that cast returns, so the sheet reflects less light overall and is still judged whiter.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Rags never bleach to a true white, and the sheet made from them keeps a yellow cast.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Papermakers added a trace of blue pigment to the stuff in the vat.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A sheet with blue pigment in it reflects less light than a sheet without any.

questions.stem: A dye works makes a standing charge of $90 for a season and then charges $6 for each skein dyed. A rival works makes no standing charge and charges $9 for each skein dyed. For how many skeins dyed in a season do the two works charge the same amount?
